title: Scoped Transitions, Folio Grids, Squiggle Type, Presence Cursors & Kanban Flow
description: Five live drops: concurrent element-scoped view transitions, a print-editorial folio grid, SVG-turbulence squiggly text, multiplayer presence cursors, and a drag-and-drop kanban board.

drops.title: Concurrent View Transitions
drops.description: Chrome 147's element-scoped startViewTransition() lets multiple elements morph independently instead of one blocking global transition.
drops.concept: document.startViewTransition() has always run one transition for the whole document — click a second trigger mid-animation and it queues behind the first. Chrome 147 shipped Element.prototype.startViewTransition(), scoping the snapshot tree to a single element so N regions of a page can be mid-morph simultaneously. This drop puts a 'Scoped' and 'Global' mode side by side on the same 6-card grid so the difference between concurrent and blocking transitions is visible, not just described.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers — "Element-scoped view transitions" blog post

interaction.mouse: Click cards to flip between summary and detail.
interaction.click: Toggle Scoped vs Global mode, watch the live transition log.
interaction.touch: Tap cards to flip; works identically to mouse.

drops.title: Editorial Folio Grid
drops.description: A print-magazine layout system with grid-template-areas spreads, drop caps, pull-quotes, and a live running folio counter.
drops.concept: Print magazines number and title their spreads in the margin so a reader always knows where they are without hunting for a page footer. This drop rebuilds that with three CSS grid-template-areas spreads (asymmetric image+text, full-bleed break with columns, sidebar footnotes), each incrementing a counter(folio) value, while an IntersectionObserver tracks which spread owns the most viewport area and writes its number into a fixed running-folio badge in real time.
drops.source: Codrops — "Between Print and Digital: The Making of MERSI's Website"

interaction.mouse: Scroll through the three spreads to watch the folio badge update.
interaction.click: Drag debug sliders to resize the drop cap and column text.
interaction.touch: Scroll normally; layout reflows per-spread via container queries below 560px.

drops.title: Squiggly Text
drops.description: SVG feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap filters swap every few dozen milliseconds, wobbling the glyphs themselves instead of drawing a mark beneath them.
drops.concept: Most emphasis techniques draw a decoration under or around a word. Aceternity's Squiggly Text instead generates a handful of feTurbulence/feDisplacementMap SVG filters up front and cycles which one is applied to the target text every stepDuration milliseconds, so the letterforms themselves visibly wobble. This drop exposes steps, step duration, displacement scale, and turbulence frequency as live sliders across three presets — subtle, medium, and wild — plus clickable status chips that pause/resume their own wobble independently.

interaction.mouse: Hover has no effect — the wobble runs continuously; click a status chip to pause it.
interaction.click: Click chips to toggle their wobble on/off.
interaction.touch: Tap chips to toggle; sliders hidden on narrow viewports.

drops.title: Presence Pointers
drops.description: Your cursor becomes a lerp-smoothed name tag exactly like Figma or Linear's multiplayer presence, alongside two simulated teammates.
drops.concept: Collaborative tools like Figma and Linear replace the OS cursor with a colored, labeled pointer that trails the real cursor position with spring/lerp smoothing, so remote collaborators feel like they're really moving through the same space. This drop hides the native cursor over a sticky-note board, renders your own custom pointer lerping toward the real pointer position every animation frame, and adds two autonomous simulated peers wandering the same board on independent sine-based paths — three pointer instances rendering concurrently.

interaction.mouse: Move over the board — your name tag follows with spring smoothing.
interaction.click: Pick a name and color from the bottom control bar.
interaction.touch: Drag on the board; touch devices skip the native-cursor hide.

drops.title: Kanban Flow Board
drops.description: A native Drag-and-Drop kanban board — HTML5 DnD on desktop, Pointer Events on touch — with every move wrapped in a view transition.
drops.concept: MDN's own HTML Drag and Drop API reference now ships a Kanban board as its canonical example: draggable cards, dragover-based drop zones, and dataTransfer carrying the card id between them. This drop reimplements that structure across three columns with a per-column WIP limit, layers a Pointer-Events-based long-press drag for touch devices where the native DnD API doesn't fire, wraps every reorder in document.startViewTransition() so cards glide to their new slot, and persists the whole board to localStorage.
drops.source: MDN Web Docs — "HTML Drag and Drop API: Kanban board" tutorial

interaction.mouse: Drag cards between columns; add/delete cards inline.
interaction.click: Click + to add a card, ✕ to delete one.
interaction.touch: Long-press a card (~160ms) then drag to another column.
